name: smoke
description: Use when the exhaust smokes (white, blue, black or grey): asks the driver the colour, then checks the systems that colour points to.
instructions: Call ask_driver {"id":"smoke_colour"}: the driver answers white, blue, black, grey or none.

Then call read_dtcs and follow the colour: black → boost, egr and dpf_regen (diesel) or fuel_trims (petrol); white → cooling (coolant loss) and glow_plugs (cold diesel); blue → oil burning, which no OBD reading shows: say a workshop must check the turbo seals, valve stem seals or rings.
Call read_live {"pids":["0105"]} once: white smoke only while cold is condensation.
interpret: White, thin and gone once warm: condensation, normal. White, thick and sweet-smelling with coolant loss: a head gasket or EGR cooler leak.
White-grey on a cold diesel: unburnt fuel from the glow plugs or injectors.
Blue: oil burning (turbo oil seals, valve stem seals, piston rings, crankcase ventilation).

Black: too much fuel or too little air: a boost leak, an EGR stuck open, a dirty air filter or a leaking injector. A puff under hard acceleration on an older diesel is normal; constant black smoke is not.
A little white-grey vapour during a DPF regeneration is normal.
None: no smoke now; ask in the report's actions when it appears (cold start, acceleration).
